prompt:
Search the web now. You are a financial fact extractor for a US-equity pre-market brief.
Brief date: Friday October 16, 2026. Topic: Company news: oil & gas, mining, chemicals and agriculture.

Window: Thursday October 15, 2026 regular session (9:30-16:00 ET) through Friday October 16, 2026 02:03 ET, including after-hours, overnight and pre-market news. Anything published after 02:03 ET on Friday October 16, 2026 is out of scope.

FIND
Every material company-specific news item for US-listed oil & gas, mining, chemicals and agriculture companies >= $1B in the window, as many as you can find: press releases, 8-K filings, executive changes, activist campaigns, legal settlements, contracts, product launches, guidance, analyst rating/PT changes (firm, old → new), and the stock move. One bullet per company.

Run multiple searches with different phrasings and dates. Prefer primary sources and wire services
(Reuters, Bloomberg, AP, CNBC, WSJ, MarketWatch, Barron's, Investopedia, company press releases, SEC
EDGAR, BLS/BEA/Census/Fed releases, FDA). For every item give the latest status as of the cutoff.

OUTPUT (markdown; no intro or conclusion). Group by ticker or topic:

## TICKER or Topic `[Category]`
- fact (source)

Category: pick from AI Compute · Memory & Interconnect · Optical & Photonics · Chip Equipment · Fab & Foundry · Wireless & Mobile · Analog & Mixed-Signal · Power & Wide-Bandgap · Test & Advanced Packaging · Specialty Materials & IP Licensing · Quantum Computing · EdgeAI · Semiconductors · AI Infrastructure · Software & SaaS · Internet & Platforms · Communications & Networking, or Macro / Commodities / Geopolitics / Crypto / Calendar /
Pharma / Energy / Retail, or a concise sector name. Bold tickers.

RULES
- Facts only. Every bullet has a specific number, name, or date. No bullet without a data point.
- End every bullet with the named source and publish time if known: (Reuters, Sep 24 07:12 ET).
  Convert every time to ET (ET = GMT-4 / UTC-4 in EDT; 09:59 GMT = 05:59 ET) before judging whether
  it is inside the window. For prices quoted several times, report the latest reading before the
  cutoff with its time.
  "Analysts said" / "reports suggest" without a name is not allowed.
- Earnings: actual vs consensus for EPS and revenue; guidance old → new.
- Analyst actions: firm, rating old → new, PT old → new.
- Mark unconfirmed items (people familiar, leaks, social media, M&A speculation) with [rumor]. A
  Bloomberg/Reuters/WSJ report citing sources is still reportable: state it and mark [report].
- If one event moved several stocks, name every stock and its move in the same bullet.
- Only facts published in the window. Older background only if it is the direct cause of a move in
  the window, labelled with its date.
- Do not interpret price action. Do not write "strong", "beat expectations", "investors cheered",
  "remains", "continues to", "well-positioned", "tailwinds". Write the number.
- Do not write bullets about what you could not find. Omit the topic instead.
- Do not drop facts to save space.
content:
## **CVX / XOM / OXY / COP / EOG** — Energy / Macro

- Brent crude fell $1.64, or 1.6%, to $104.42 per barrel and WTI fell $0.98, or 1.0%, to $94.11 in early Thursday trading; the report attributed the move to Hormuz attacks and U.S. sanctions relief (Reuters, Oct 15 01:30 ET).[9]

- The International Energy Agency said members would accelerate the release of remaining emergency oil stocks, including more than 20 million barrels of diesel “as soon as possible”; about 330 million barrels of the more than 400 million barrels pledged in March had been released as of Oct. 15 (Reuters, Oct 15 11:21 ET).[5]

- The United States informally urged IEA members to commit to releasing at least another 100 million barrels, while officials had not yet submitted a formal proposal; Reuters said it could not independently verify the Bloomberg report [rumor][report] (Reuters, Oct 15 08:32 ET).[10]

## **VLO / MPC / PSX / TTE** — Refining and Chemicals / Energy

- TotalEnergies said its downstream business was expected to produce exceptional third-quarter results after refining margins increased amid supply disruptions and export restrictions; the company-specific report also cited stronger gas prices and oil-and-gas trading (Dow Jones, Oct 15 15:08 ET).[2]

- RBC Capital Markets analyst Biraj Borkhataria cut TotalEnergies’ estimated third-quarter adjusted net income to $9.2 billion from $9.3 billion and raised estimated operating cash flow to $12.3 billion from $12.2 billion (Dow Jones, Oct 15 03:40 ET).[2]

## **LNG / VG** — Energy

- Venture Global was reported to be pursuing gas-fired power generation at its facilities to supply electricity to data centers, extending its LNG infrastructure into power generation [report] (Dow Jones, Oct 15 15:08 ET).[2]

## **CENX / CMC** — Metals and Mining

- Commercial Metals reported fourth-quarter net income of $212.5 million, or $1.91 per share, compared with $151.8 million, or $1.35 per share, a year earlier; the report cited expanding metal margins and demand in its construction-solutions unit (Dow Jones, Oct 15 15:08 ET).[2]

## **Commodity Markets** — Agriculture

- Chinese state-owned buyers purchased 8–10 Panamax cargoes of U.S. soybeans for December shipment at premiums of $3.10–$3.20 over January futures, marking the first major purchases since the September Trump–Xi summit (Reuters, Oct 15 01:30 ET).[9]

- Chicago wheat futures rose 0.4% after Argus reduced its Russia wheat-production forecast to 79.5 million metric tons, a three-year low (Reuters, Oct 15 01:30 ET).[9]

## **Energy / Mining / Geopolitics**

- U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent called for World Bank reforms that would permit upstream oil and gas financing and support deep-sea critical-minerals mining; the Treasury statement said the bank should take a technology-neutral approach to energy (Reuters, Oct 15, time not reported).[6]

- Saudi Aramco offered traders additional crude cargoes for spot delivery to Europe between late October and mid-November; Reuters said volumes, grades, pricing terms, and destinations were not disclosed, and the company had not responded by publication [report] (Reuters, Oct 15, time not reported).[3]

- A report said President Donald Trump’s Oct. 14 Greenland oil-and-minerals remarks did not correspond to a drilling or mining agreement; Greenland’s deputy mining minister said U.S. companies remained “very far away” from large-scale activity, and Greenland’s 2026 drilling window was reportedly delayed until winter 2027 at the earliest [report] (Discovery Alert, Oct 15, time not reported).[7]
